description: The `signed` envelope in wire version 2 (SPEC §3.2.2, §4.3). b is the body as JCS text; the signature input is JCS(["tieroute/v2", t, b]); hashes are SHA-256 of JCS of the whole envelope. `signed` is the auth body for POST auth/session, signed by a device: k is the device's 32-byte Ed25519 component, and s is a 3,373-byte composite signature that verifies with the device's composite key (`signer.public_hex`, found in the chain). `composite` breaks that signature down (see composite.json). `message_key_signed` is an app-message signed by a message key: k is the 32-byte message key and s a 64-byte Ed25519 signature. Every envelope in `reject` must be refused.
notice: Test vectors for Tieroute wire version 2 (SPEC version 2.0, draft). These keys are public: never use them for anything real.

reject.note: the auth envelope with an extra member: the envelope is closed (SPEC §4.3)
an Ed25519-only signature by the device's Ed25519 component over the signature input: a composite signature is required, with no fallback (SPEC §3.2.2)
the composite signature with one bit of the ML-DSA component flipped: both components must verify (SPEC §3.2.1)
the composite signature with one bit of the Ed25519 component flipped
each component signed over the bare signature input instead of M': each verifies alone, but not as a composite
a composite signature over the version 1 signature input JCS(["tieroute/v1", t, b])
